title: Cap. VIII Arg. 2: Rom. 9 — reprobation called hatred of Esau
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, they try to demonstrate that foresighted demerits are the cause of reprobation (which may seem strange to someone) from the very disputation of the Apostle in Romans 9. Where it seems to us that he establishes the contrary opinion. First from this, that the Apostle calls this reprobation hatred; Esau I have hated: But God hates no one except for the cause of sin.
pass_b_english: Second, they try to prove foresighted demerits are the cause of reprobation — oddly enough — from Paul's own debate in Romans 9, where we take him to establish the opposite. First: the Apostle calls this reprobation hatred — Esau I hated — and God hates no one except for sin.
source_text: Secundo, conantur demonstrare praevisa demerita esse causam reprobationis (quod mirum alicui videri potest) ex ipsa disputatione Apostoli Rom. ix. Ubi nobis videtur contrariam sententiam stabilire. Primo ex eo quod Apostolus vocat hanc reprobationem odium; Esau odio habui: Deus autem neminem odit nisi peccati causa.
